DECIDED 2026-10-04 by the user: ids keep recycling for now, revisited once this lane lands. Known cause: next_id takes the max over open rows and the records they hold, and a closed top-level row leaves the file holding neither, so its number is free (t31, t32, t33 and t34 have each been used twice). The shapes that would fix it without a second store: a time-based id (t<unix_ms>), or a close that leaves something a number can be read from.

content: The live TUI smoke test for S2 and S3, deferred so it exercises both at once: build a fresh kcode, in a scratch repo add rows with the todo tool (two roots, one child naming a root as parent, one row blocked by another), confirm the pinned list shows id + words, the child indented, the blocked row marked and no card/page/pips/roster surface; run /auto (or spawn a worker) so a member takes a row and its glyph animates with @name, model and age; stop the holder mid-row and the row goes red; close a blocker and the mark clears. The numbered steps are in docs/plans/task-flow.md under The live check for S2 and S3. Gate: each observed screen matches, step by step.

The improve and refactor commands read the work file in the client, which rule 1 forbids (the server is the only reader; the client renders the rows it is pushed). Ten crate::todo::load_tasks calls: four in remote/key_handling.rs (the /improve and /refactor resume and stop arms) and six in commands_improve.rs (build_improve_resume_prompt's callers and both format_*_status). Options: read the app's pushed rows (app.pinned_todo_rows()) instead, which is right when the improve session is the attached one, or move the status/list logic server-side and have the client request it. The catch is that the improve target can be a session this client is not attached to, so the pushed rows may not be the right session's; the fix has to name the session it wants rows for. Gate: no crate::todo::load_tasks in kcode-tui, and the improve/refactor status tests still pass.
